sources.description:
亞洲影帝柯俊雄紀念肖像

這張黑白肖像捕捉了柯俊雄的溫暖微笑與自信神情，他身著西裝、打著領帶，略帶顆粒感的影像質感營造出濃厚的懷舊氛圍。作為首位獲得亞洲影展最佳男主角的台灣演員，柯俊雄在1967年憑《寂寞的17歲》奠定影帝地位，並在往後數十年中以多變的角色形象和精湛演技贏得無數獎項。

2015年柯俊雄因肺癌病逝，享年70歲。為了紀念他的傳奇一生，妻子蔡青樺與金鐘主持人陳凱倫合作，歷時三年並獲文化部支持，製作了紀錄片《柯俊雄電影人生》。首映會於中午舉行，吸引了演藝圈好友與眾多戲迷到場，共同回顧他豐富的作品與傲人成就。

sources.description:
Ko Chun-hsiung Portrait

This formal studio portrait features veteran Taiwanese actor Ko Chun-hsiung seated against a dark, neutral background. He wears a vertically striped shirt and rests his hand thoughtfully on his chin, meeting the camera with a calm, introspective gaze. The lighting accentuates his facial contours and the fine details of his attire, conveying a sense of dignity and poise.

The image is the first in an eleven-photo gallery on the 360 Baike website, which offers navigation controls and links to view additional details about each photograph in the Ko Chun-hsiung album.

Tribute to Ke Junxiong

Veteran actor Ke Junxiong is portrayed seated in a dark suit against a simple light background, his expression composed and dignified. sources.title: Actor | Ko Chun-hsiung
sources.description:
Ko Chun-hsiung

Ko Chun-hsiung (柯俊雄), born January 15, 1945 in Tainan, Southern Taiwan, rose from a teenage actor in a Taigi film to one of Taiwan’s most iconic screen presences. Over a fifty-year career, he appeared in more than a hundred films and several television series, earning three Golden Horse Awards and becoming the first Taiwanese actor to win Best Actor at the Asia Pacific Film Festival in 1968 for "Lonely Seventeen." Known for his debonair looks and gentlemanly roles in Chiung Yao romance adaptations, he also delivered memorable performances in war films such as "Eight Hundred Heroes" and "Storm Over the Yangtse River."

sources.description:
Smiling Couple at Entrance

A black-and-white photograph shows a man and woman standing together in front of a revolving glass door. The man wears a dark overcoat and tie, while the woman sports a fur-trimmed coat, both smiling directly at the camera. The setting suggests an indoor lobby or terminal, with overhead lights reflecting off the glass behind them.

This image accompanies a Yahoo Autos news article about Taiwanese actor Ko Chun‑hsiung’s health and his daughter’s decision not to attend his funeral service. Although published in an automotive section, the article focuses on celebrity family matters rather than vehicles.
